subject: CAIQ evidence: deploy-chain narrative and secrets attestation
messages:
From: Alex Martin <alex@auditpartnertools.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: SIG Assessment Team <sig@assessments.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ evidence: deploy-chain narrative and secrets attestation

Hi Priyom,

We're kicking off the CAIQ-oriented SIG review for FinAnalytics (requested by their compliance team). To complete our mapping against the Secure SDLC sections we need a concise set of artifacts and a short narrative that ties them together. Specifically we need: 

- Deploy-chain narrative (how code moves from repo -> CI -> artifact registry -> prod), including approvals and rollback path.
- Evidence of CI/CD controls (pipeline configuration, PR gating, branch protection, sample pipeline run logs).
- Code review policy + a representative PR review log export.
- Secrets management controls (ephemeral credentialing, vault/KMS usage, rotation schedule).
- Change management trail for a recent production change (ticket + approval history).

If possible, upload artifacts to a shared folder and reply with links. A one-paragraph mapping (2-4 bullets) of how each artifact satisfies the CAIQ questions would be ideal.

Timing: FinAnalytics is aiming to close this review next week; can you share initial artifacts by end of day Friday 20 Jun?

Thanks,
Alex Martin
Principal Assessor
Audit Partners

--
Note: We'll accept redacted logs for any PII-sensitive fields.
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <alex@auditpartnertools.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence: deploy-chain narrative and secrets attestation

Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping in Jordan (Platform) and Irene (Security ops) to collect the artifacts. We'll assemble a short mapping doc and drop the artifacts into a shared Drive folder.

Quick notes / plan:
- Jordan: can you export a sample PR review log, the CI runbook (redacted where needed), and a pipeline run snapshot?
- Irene: can you include the secrets rotation schedule, KMS key IDs (no private keys), and the keystore rotation attestation if available?

We'll aim to have the initial package uploaded by EOD Friday 20 Jun. If anything will slip, we'll notify you by Thursday.

Priyom
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Martin <alex@auditpartnertools.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence: deploy-chain narrative and secrets attestation

Folks — uploading the first tranche now and documenting how each item maps to the CAIQ Secure SDLC checks. Links and attachments below.

Deliverables uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-example-evidence-folder
Attachments included in this email: pr-review-sample.csv, ci-runbook.pdf, secrets-rotation-snapshot.txt

Summary mapping (short):
1) Deploy-chain narrative: our code flow is GitHub -> PR + branch protections -> CI (Jenkins pipelines orchestrated via terraform) -> container build -> image pushed to internal registry (artifactory) -> deploy via ArgoCD with automated canary policies. Approvals: PR approvals required by two reviewers; production deploys require an automated gating job plus an on-call manual approval for hotfixes. Rollback: ArgoCD rollback to previous image tag; documented in CI runbook (see section 4).

2) CI/CD controls: ci-runbook.pdf contains pipeline config snippets (branch protections, required status checks, mandatory linters), and an exported pipeline run (redacted) shows required steps and gating. PR gating: required reviewers, no merge without green checks.

3) Code review evidence: pr-review-sample.csv is an export of PR metadata (PR id, reviewers, approval timestamps, merge commit). This is a representative slice — redacted commit IDs are replaced with pseudonyms.

4) Secrets management: secrets-rotation-snapshot.txt summarizes vault roles, rotation cadence (30/90/365 days depending on secret class), and use of AWS KMS for envelope encryption. We rotate ephemeral CI tokens every 12 hours via short-lived STS credentials.

5) Change management: linked Jira ticket SUP-4521 shows a production rollout with approval audit trail: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-4521 (permissioned link).

Attachments: pr-review-sample.csv (sample export, redacted), ci-runbook.pdf (pipeline conf + runbook), secrets-rotation-snapshot.txt (rotation cadence & roles).

If you need a signed attestation for key rotation we can route a DocuSign to the infra manager — let me know and I'll raise it today.

Jordan Blake
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs:
- pr-review-sample.csv (CSV, 45 KB)
- ci-runbook.pdf (PDF, 310 KB)
- secrets-rotation-snapshot.txt (TXT, 6 KB)
From: Alex Martin <alex@auditpartnertools.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence: deploy-chain narrative and secrets attestation

Jordan / Priyom — thanks, that looks like a good first package and the mapping is exactly what we need. Two quick follow-ups before we close the ticket with FinAnalytics: 

1) Keystore rotation attestation: we need a signed statement confirming the last rotation event for the keystore(s) that protect production signing keys (date + approver). A DocuSign flow is fine.
2) Pipeline run logs: we took the sample CSV but would like one full pipeline run log (redacted of any secrets) that shows the gating checks and artifact promotion steps.

If you can route the keystore attestation to the infra manager for signature and upload the single run log to the same Drive folder, we should be able to finalize the CAIQ mapping tomorrow.

I'll mark SUP-4521 as the reference in our assessment notes.

Thanks — much appreciated.
Alex Martin
Principal Assessor
Audit Partners
